title: 1953 British Everest expedition: approach to Base Camp
timeSemantics: Dates are expedition narrative dates in 1953. No UTC times are inferred. Local wall-clock times remain source times; coordinates are modern approximate georeferences for map display, not surveyed 1953 fixes.

weatherCoverage.purpose: Provide historical weather context for every day in the approach and summit window; weather values are retrospective/modelled context, not expedition observations.
weatherCoverage.joinRule: Join weather by calendar date only unless a source supplies a clock and timezone. Do not fill missing expedition dates with invented observations.

routeKnownVsInferred.known: The primary narrative identifies the sequence from Bhadgaon through the Dudh Kosi, Namche and Thyangboche to the Khumbu/Base Camp, and describes later acclimatization sorties and camp work.
routeKnownVsInferred.inferred: Point coordinates, connecting lines between named places, and unlisted daily stops are approximate map geometry only. Ship, aircraft, rail, and border-crossing legs before Nepal are omitted unless the source gives them explicitly.
routeKnownVsInferred.campCoordinatePolicy: Camp II, Camp III and Advanced Base coordinates are omitted here: the cited narratives give camp names/elevations but not survey coordinates, and map products disagree.

milestones.event: The main party reached Bombay before travelling overland toward Nepal; the source does not establish the exact Nepal arrival date.
milestones.source: Charles Wylie, Himalayan Journal 18/1, assembly section

milestones.participants: first march-out party: 9 sahibs, Tenzing, 16 climbing Sherpas and about 180 coolies
milestones.event: The first party began the march toward Thyangboche.
milestones.source: John Hunt and Michael Westmacott, Alpine Journal narrative, p. 107; reproduced in Himalayan Journal 18/1
milestones.evidenceLocator: HTML line 42; spelling ‘nth’ is an OCR/rendering artifact for 11th

milestones.participants: second march-out party and support porters
milestones.event: The second party followed the first; the source groups 10–11 March as the Bhadgaon departure window rather than assigning every porter to a separate dated track.
milestones.source: Charles Wylie, Himalayan Journal 18/1, approach section

milestones.event: A contemporary report placed the party at Namche Bazar during the approach; the primary expedition narrative confirms Namche as an approach waypoint but does not date this stop.
The first and second parties reached Thyangboche on successive days; this is not a single-date arrival for the entire expedition.
milestones.source: John Hunt and Michael Westmacott, Alpine Journal narrative, p. 109; expedition chronology cross-check
milestones.evidenceLocator: Alpine Journal p. 109; indexed expedition chronology

milestones.place: Thyangboche to upper Khumbu/Imja acclimatization routes
milestones.event: The parties left Thyangboche in three groups for the first acclimatization period; destinations diverged, so this record does not draw one shared route.
milestones.source: Hunt and Westmacott, Alpine Journal narrative, p. 109

milestones.event: The parties were back at Thyangboche for two days of rest and reorganization before setting out again.

The Himalayan Database chronology lists 12 April for Base Camp; the narrative separately describes parties moving up the Imja and Khumbu glacier, so this date is retained as a cross-check rather than presented as a uniquely sourced establishment moment.
milestones.source: Himalayan Database EVER53101 chronology; Hunt narrative
milestones.evidenceLocator: Himalayan Database expedition chronology; narrative context in HJ HTML lines 72-74

milestones.participants: Hunt, Band and Hillary reconnaissance party; support teams
milestones.place: Camp III / head of the Khumbu Icefall
milestones.event: Camp III is described at 20,200 ft; the route into the Western Cwm was explored on 22 April.
The source set describes Advanced Base and subsequent route development toward the Lhotse Face and South Col; no survey coordinate is asserted here.
milestones.source: Hunt and Westmacott, Alpine Journal narrative; Himalayan Database chronology
milestones.evidenceLocator: Alpine Journal narrative; date is a chronology cross-check, not a quoted establishment date

openQuestions: The cited sources do not provide a complete day-by-day list of every march stop between Bhadgaon, Namche, Thyangboche and Base Camp.

The primary narrative supports 26–27 March for the two Thyangboche arrivals; references to an Imja opening on 22 March should not be merged into that arrival milestone without a source-specific party and context.
The sources do not establish the expedition clock's UTC offset; preserve local wall-clock semantics for later timed climbing entries.
Modern coordinates for historical camps have moved or differ by map datum and glacier change; only named places with defensible georeferences are mapped, and disputed camp coordinates are omitted.
The approach of individual climbers diverged from the main portering parties; do not collapse all participants into one track without a source-specific account.
